headline: Twice the plants, twice the cash flow, and future capacity revenue sold to buy back stock: Talen turns AI power demand into cash flow per share

points.t: After buying Freedom, Guernsey and three gas plants in June, generation rose from 11.1 TWh to 23.9 TWh and the capacity factor from 57% to 75%.

points.b: Borrowing from the future to buy back stock
points.t: Sold about $1.5B of 2027/28 and 2028/29 PJM capacity revenue for $1.3B and, with cash on hand, funded a $1.5B accelerated buyback; the share count is down to about 43.5M.

points.b: The stock has already come down
points.t: It closed at $332.99 before the report, 26% below the 52-week high of $449.84 and 13% below the end-June $384.

reaction: Stock: closed at $332.99 before the report and was about $342.50 (+2.9%) before the open on 3 Nov (Investing.com). Revenue beat, the 2026 guidance midpoint held, and the first 2027 guidance calls for EBITDA +26% and free cash flow +27%. On the day (3 Nov) it closed at $357.28, +7.3%, against +3.0% for the power peers average; the next day (4 Nov) it closed at $326.78, −8.5%, against −10.3%. 4 Nov was the first day after the midterms, when the AI chain split: cloud companies rose while power, cooling and construction stocks fell hard. Consensus from Investing.com: revenue $1.29B.

segments.title: Where the money comes from and goes
segments.bridgeT: From adjusted EBITDA to free cash flow
segments.take: Two-thirds of EBITDA became free cash flow; the biggest deduction is interest, because the plant acquisitions were financed with debt.

rows.why: A Pennsylvania nuclear station that earns the nuclear production tax credit (PTC). In 2025 it signed a long-term power contract with Amazon (AWS) of up to 1.92 GW through 2042, with a minimum volume that steps up each year. Nuclear is Talen's most direct link to data centers.

Gas and coal units in PJM, plus plants in Ohio, Indiana and Montana. Purchases over the past year of Freedom, Guernsey, Lawrenceburg, Waterford and Darby doubled the fleet. More than 10 GW cleared the 2028/29 PJM capacity auction at $325/MW-day.

segments.note: The company reports a single segment and does not disclose revenue by plant. Shares are by installed capacity. GAAP net income of $138M was below last year's $207M, mainly because of a $190M unrealized loss on commodity derivatives and interest on acquisition financing.

extras.title: Where it sits in the AI loop
extras.take: Talen sits at the very top of the loop: generation. AI data centers need large amounts of steady power, so power and capacity prices in PJM (the eastern US grid, home to northern Virginia's data center cluster) have risen, and Talen's plants are worth more. It is the same kind of company as Vistra and Constellation.

items.b: Nuclear straight to a data center
items.w: The long-term Susquehanna contract locks part of the nuclear output to Amazon at a price that does not float with the market. It is the template for “behind-the-meter” supply (a data center next to the plant).

Data centers are pushing PJM's forecast peak up fast, and capacity auctions have cleared at high prices for several years. Capacity revenue is the most certain part of Talen's cash flow over the next two years, but two of those years have already been sold for cash.
About 80% of Q4, about 70% of 2027 and about 35% of 2028 is hedged. The upside: 2027 guidance is fairly stable. The downside: if prices keep rising, Talen captures less than its peers.

After the acquisitions and the accelerated buyback, net debt is about 5x 2026 EBITDA, above the 3.5x target; the plan is to bring it down through 2027 EBITDA growth. If power prices fall, high leverage amplifies the stock's swings.

Capacity price caps, “bring your own generation” rules for data centers, and regulatory approval of behind-the-meter supply all affect how much power Talen can sell and at what price. In 2024 the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) rejected an expanded behind-the-meter arrangement for Amazon at Susquehanna.

extras.title: Where growth comes from
extras.take: Talen's own target is free cash flow per share: a fleet twice the size brings more EBITDA, and buybacks keep shrinking the share count. 2027 growth comes mainly from a full year of the new plants.

items.b: Volume: a full year of new plants
items.w: The three plants bought in June contributed only part of the year; 2027 is a full year, the main reason for 2027 EBITDA +26%.
Most power prices from 2028 on are not locked in, so PJM supply and demand set Talen's ceiling and floor.
After the ASR, $1.5B remains on the SRP through end-2028. At today's price that buys about 4.5M more shares, about 10%.
The 2027 AFCF midpoint of $1.625B over about 42.6M shares (after the ASR) is about $38 a share, more than 40% above 2026's roughly $26.6. Company materials put 2028 at about $48 a share.
PJM capacity or power prices falling; outages at the nuclear station or big units; rules that limit behind-the-meter supply; higher rates making refinancing costlier; more borrowing to fund buybacks.

valuation.take: On 2027 guidance, about 9x EV/EBITDA and under 9x free cash flow per share (a free cash flow yield of about 11%). It looks cheap because most power prices are unhedged, leverage is about 5x, and two years of capacity revenue have already been spent.

scenarios.note: Bear: PJM capacity and power prices fall and the unhedged 65% sells cheaply; base: near the top of 2027 guidance plus modest growth, a little below the roughly $48 a share in company materials; bull: prices keep rising and a new data center contract is signed. Deductions from EBITDA to AFCF (capex, interest, taxes, pensions) are about $1.15B a year per 2027 guidance, a bit more tax in the bull case. These assumptions are ours and are not forecasts.

pricezone.sub: 2028 AFCF per share × our multiple; price at the 2 Nov close (before the report)
pricezone.why: The price is above the zone: buying at $333, the base case gains about 26% and the bear case loses about 25%, a reward/risk of about 1.0. At the $305 top of the zone the reward/risk is about 2; at the $270 low end, about 7. The multiples are low (8–11x free cash flow) because most prices are unhedged and leverage is high; multiples for this group have swung widely with power prices. The $248 bear price is below the 52-week low of $279.77.
pricezone.note: Under review: after the midterms, rules on direct supply to data centers and PJM capacity prices may face more scrutiny. First check data center contracts in the Vistra (6 Nov) and Constellation (9 Nov) results.

history.title: Against its own past
history.sub: P/S (TTM revenue), quarter ends; relisted after its May 2023 reorganization, so only 8 comparable quarter ends
history.note: About 3.7x now, the lowest since relisting, against a median of about 5x. One reason is that acquisitions doubled revenue while the stock didn't keep up. Talen has no steady GAAP profit (large derivative marks) and an incomplete EBITDA history, so we compare P/S. We calculate it from SEC quarterly revenue, share counts and quarter-end closes.

cash.title: Cash generation
cash.sub: Adjusted free cash flow per quarter, $M
cash.note: Interest payments were $149M this quarter, against $36M a year ago. 2027 guidance has $585–615M of interest payments, up from $460–480M in 2026. On 1 Oct the $1.3B from the capacity monetization plus cash funded the first ASR delivery.
